scope: Physical-address catalog capacity for private and published memory objects uses byte-only admission from memory_capability_nodes. The complete catalog retains its original backing-source class and allocation through moves, consumed release identities and uncertain physical cleanup. Numeric limits, node counts, physical completion rules and the statistics/SDK ABI are unchanged.
artifact_note: Runtime Rust sources were frozen before all campaigns. Later documentation edits alter tracked-diff identities; source and archived artifact hashes identify the code exercised. Service sources and SDK/ABI are unchanged; staged signed bundles were reused and runners regenerated signed security fixtures.

policy.vector_charge: [pages * size_of(PAddr), 0]; exact capacity is reserved before allocation and checked afterwards
policy.pool_inventory: 22 existing pools; statistics payload version 9; no new pool or unit
policy.capture: ChargedFrames captures platform_identity(owner.id()) == Some(exact_handle) before page/object reservation and preparation. ObjectStorage and FrameVector receive this same captured class. Copy preserves the existing source backing sponsorship separately from destination capability metadata; move transfers the same vector and charge. Later promotion or ASID reuse cannot reclassify refunds.
policy.preparation: Admit object storage, then full exact catalog capacity, before physical allocator entry. The constructor owns vector and charge before allocation; allocated constructor rejection frees its buffer before refund. The complete backing preparation then cancels its object node and original page/object reservation. Quota or size denial returns ResourceLimit; allocation failure returns FrameAllocFailed. No unchecked growth API is exposed.
policy.retention: FrameVector uses inert ManuallyDrop storage within complete backing custody. Popping physical identities preserves allocated capacity and its full original charge. Empty length does not establish physical completion. Failure/abandonment retains vector, object node, both budgets and terminal fence without physical replay.
policy.release: Confirmed physical completion permits consuming finish; the actual buffer is freed before its metadata reservation drops. Published object cleanup also frees its object node before returning the original physical charge. Unused empty preparation is explicitly disposed only through the existing cancellation path.
policy.decision: Keep numeric defaults. A maximum catalog requests 128 KiB; the additional 24-byte inline owner needs no holder allocation and is included in the measured 248-byte object-node layout. Catalogs compete with existing metadata for same-class bytes, but these real-pressure and native controls pass without increased limits. Larger object maxima or measured mixed-workload pressure can justify co-scaling central metadata/snapshot budgets. Independent ceilings do not promise simultaneous RAM fit or fairness.
policy.profile_validation: Compile-time validation requires one maximum object catalog to fit the ordinary memory_capability_nodes byte ceiling, alongside the existing snapshot-buffer bound. Default and larger profiles execute actual policy tests; an incompatible catalog profile fails compilation.
